purpose: Historical legally documented monetary outcomes, not a measure of toxic harm, fault, mortality or an additive company score.

USD.method: US CPI-U all items, U.S. city average, annual mean (NSA); reference 2025. 2025 BLS annual average omits October due to the federal funding lapse.

BRL.method: IBGE IPCA calendar-year Dec/Dec rates compounded after nominal base year through December 2025. The 2021 agreement was signed in February; December-2021 convention is only a standardized comparator, not a contractual indexation calculation.

cases.hazard: Mine-tailings dam failure / watershed and communities
cases.disposition: Judicial agreement; separate individual and criminal proceedings remain distinct

obligation.kind: Total agreed collective reparation package; includes works performed, future work and transfers

payment.detail: Minas Gerais environmental authority reported R$18.2bn already paid toward different agreement obligations after one year; covers multiple payment/implementation periods. This is a dated historical lower bound, not a current 2026 total. Separately, Vale's June 2026 investor reporting discloses US$15.172bn of total cumulative Brumadinho-related outlays since 2019 across a broader scope, including dam decommissioning, individual/emergency compensation and other work. That broader figure is not the cash paid under this exact 2021 agreement and must not be substituted for, added to, or currency-converted into this R$18.2bn historical observation.

cases.notes: Agreement contains both duties to perform works and duties to transfer funds. Paid figure and package overlap; they must never be added. Multi-year cash has no single valid inflation base year.
